main_text.p: delabantur, qui potius Cacodæmoni quam Deo aufcultant, qui potius superstitioni quam religioni intenti sunt. Hanc fallacem ac periculosam eventuum certitudinem passim pii observant, meritoque ingemiscunt: dum vana passim, ut olim sic etiamnum, divinationes instituuntur, vel ex avium cantu aut volatu earundem, vel ex pastu pullorum, extorum infpectione, & cafu utcunque contingentibus portentis; dum per fraudes & imposturas diabolicas dies horaque felices infelicesve dehignantur, pro negotiis gerendis; dum per interrogata de rebus incertis dubiisve respondetur; quis fuerit furatus rem forte amissam? quo fur se abduxerit? dum per cribri rotationem, per annuli motum, per fortilegia, per alias sexcentas diabolicas fraudes & artes, indicia petuntur; dum per horas natales de fortuna ac moribus, vivendi moriendique forte inquiritur; dum incantationibus, vel characteribus sive signatis duntaxat sive collo appensis, aliaque multiplici Cacodæmonum arte, nec in Scriptura nec in Natura fundamentum habente, agritudines sanantur, venena depelluntur, mali spiritus

page.notes: Page is slightly cut at the right and bottom edges; the last words are partly cropped. Some words were read with uncertainty, e.g. "delabantur", "dehignantur" and "sexcentas" (read as printed "sexcentas" may be "sexcentas"); the last line "spiritus" is partly cropped and may be incomplete. The text is set in a font with long s, which has been transcribed as plain s.
